title: Parables of the Kingdom

questions.question: In the Parable of the Sower, what happened to the seeds that fell along the path?
options: The birds came and devoured them
They sprang up quickly but were scorched by the sun
Thorns grew up and choked them
questions.correctAnswer: The birds came and devoured them
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:4 (ESV): "And as he sowed, some seeds fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured them."

questions.question: What do the seeds sown among thorns represent in Jesus' explanation?
options: The one who hears the word, but the cares of the world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and it proves unfruitful
The one who receives it with joy but has no root
The one who does not understand it and the evil one snatches it away
The one who bears a hundredfold
questions.correctAnswer: The one who hears the word, but the cares of the world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and it proves unfruitful
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:22 (ESV): "As for what was sown among thorns, this is the one who hears the word, but the cares of the world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and it proves unfruitful."

questions.question: When the disciples asked Jesus why He spoke in parables, what was His reason?
options: "To you it has been given to know the secrets of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given."
"Because my Father spoke in parables also."
questions.correctAnswer: "To you it has been given to know the secrets of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given."
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:11 (ESV): "And he answered them, 'To you it has been given to know the secrets of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.'"

questions.question: Jesus speaking in parables fulfills the prophecy: "I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter what has been hidden since... "
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:35 (ESV): "...what has been hidden since the foundation of the world." (Quoting Psalm 78:2)

questions.question: In the parable of the Weeds among the Wheat, an enemy comes and sows weeds. When the servants ask if they should pull up the weeds, what does the master say?
options: "No, lest in gathering the weeds you root up the wheat along with them. Let both grow together until the harvest."
"Yes, gather them immediately to save the wheat."
"Hire more servants to sort them daily."
questions.correctAnswer: "No, lest in gathering the weeds you root up the wheat along with them. Let both grow together until the harvest."
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:29-30 (ESV): "But he said, 'No, lest in gathering the weeds you root up the wheat along with them. Let both grow together until the harvest...'"

questions.question: In Jesus' explanation of the Parable of the Weeds, who sows the good seed?
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:37 (ESV): "He answered, 'The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.'"

questions.question: In Jesus' explanation, who is the enemy that sows the weeds?
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:39 (ESV): "and the enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels."

questions.question: The kingdom of heaven is compared to a grain of what tiny seed, which grows larger than all garden plants and becomes a tree?
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:31-32 (ESV): "The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his field. It is the smallest of all seeds..."

questions.question: The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of what, until it was all leavened?
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:33 (ESV): "The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, till it was all leavened."

questions.question: The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. What does a man do when he finds it?
options: He covers it up, goes in his joy and sells all that he has and buys that field
He takes the treasure and flees the country
He reports it to the king
He shares it equally with his neighbors
questions.correctAnswer: He covers it up, goes in his joy and sells all that he has and buys that field
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:44 (ESV): "The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and covered up. Then in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field."

questions.question: The kingdom of heaven is also like a merchant in search of fine pearls. Upon finding one pearl of great value, what did he do?
options: He went and sold all that he had and bought it
He traded his business for it
He stole it in the night
He borrowed money from the moneylenders to acquire it
questions.correctAnswer: He went and sold all that he had and bought it
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:45-46 (ESV): "On finding one pearl of great value, he went and sold all that he had and bought it."

questions.question: In the Parable of the Net, what happens when the net is drawn ashore?
options: The good fish are sorted into containers, but the bad are thrown away
All fish are sold in the market
The net breaks due to the sheer number of fish
questions.correctAnswer: The good fish are sorted into containers, but the bad are thrown away
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:47-48 (ESV): "...they sat down and sorted the good into containers but threw away the bad."

questions.question: Who will the angels separate the evil from at the end of the age, and throw into the fiery furnace?
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:49 (ESV): "So it will be at the end of the age. The angels will come out and separate the evil from the righteous"

questions.question: Jesus compares an instructed scribe in the kingdom to a master of a house who brings out of his treasure what?
options: What is new and what is old
questions.correctAnswer: What is new and what is old
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:52 (ESV): "...is like a master of a house, who brings out of his treasure what is new and what is old."

questions.question: When Jesus returned to His hometown of Nazareth, why did He not do many mighty works there?
options: Because Herod warned Him to leave
Because His hour had not yet come
Because the crowds were too large
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:58 (ESV): "And he did not do many mighty works there, because of their unbelief."

key_verse_text: "The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and covered up. Then in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field."
